_note: Interview question bank by role type. Add your own questions here; each role's 'match' words pick it automatically from a job title.

questions.q: Tell me about yourself.
questions.tip: 90 seconds: present role, 2 proof points, why this job now.

questions.q: Why do you want to work here?
questions.tip: One reason about the company, one about the team or product, one about your growth.

questions.q: Why are you leaving your current role?
questions.tip: Stay positive: what you're moving toward, not away from.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you failed.
questions.tip: Real failure, your share of it, what you changed afterwards.

questions.q: Describe a conflict with a colleague and how you resolved it.
questions.tip: Show you sought to understand first, then the outcome.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you led without formal authority.
questions.tip: How you built alignment: data, a shared goal, small wins.

questions.q: Describe a time you had to make a decision with incomplete information.
questions.tip: What you knew, what you assumed, how you limited the risk.

questions.q: What's an accomplishment you're most proud of?
questions.tip: Pick one with a number and a clear 'I' role.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you received tough feedback.
questions.tip: What it was, how you reacted, what changed.

questions.q: How do you prioritise when everything is urgent?
questions.tip: Name a framework, then a real example.

questions.q: Where do you see yourself in three years?
questions.tip: Ambitious but tied to this role's growth path.

questions.q: What are your salary expectations?
questions.tip: Give a researched range; anchor on the role's scope.

questions.q: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.tip: Always yes: ask about success metrics, team challenges, how decisions are made.

questions.q: Pick a product you love. How would you improve it?
questions.tip: User segment → pain point → solutions → prioritise → metric.

questions.q: How would you measure the success of [our core feature]?
questions.tip: North-star metric, 2-3 input metrics, a guardrail metric.

questions.q: Our key metric dropped 10% last week. How do you investigate?
questions.tip: Check data issues first, then segment by time, platform, cohort, funnel step.

questions.q: How do you decide what goes on the roadmap?
questions.tip: Impact vs effort, strategy fit, evidence; show a real trade-off.

questions.q: Design a product for [user group] to solve [problem].
questions.tip: Clarify goal, pick a segment, list needs, sketch MVP, define metric.

questions.q: Tell me about a product you launched end to end.
questions.tip: Problem, insight, what you shipped, result with numbers.

questions.q: How do you work with engineers who disagree with your priorities?
questions.tip: Shared context, data, willingness to change your mind.

questions.q: Should we build, buy or partner for [capability]?
questions.tip: Core vs context, time to market, cost, control.

questions.q: How would you price a new feature?
questions.tip: Value to user, competitor anchors, willingness-to-pay test.

questions.q: Estimate the market size for [product] in [country].
questions.tip: Top-down and bottom-up; state assumptions out loud.

questions.q: When would you NOT use AI in a product?
questions.tip: When accuracy, cost or trust requirements aren't met; show judgement.

questions.q: Walk me through a system you designed. What would you change now?
questions.tip: Requirements, components, trade-offs, bottlenecks, lessons.

questions.q: Design a URL shortener / rate limiter / news feed.
questions.tip: Requirements → API → data model → scale → failure modes.

questions.q: How do you debug a production issue you can't reproduce locally?
questions.tip: Logs, metrics, traces, bisecting changes, feature flags.

questions.q: Tell me about a hard bug you fixed.
questions.tip: Symptom, hypotheses, the clue that cracked it, prevention.

questions.q: How do you decide between a quick fix and a proper refactor?
questions.tip: Blast radius, deadlines, tech-debt ticket with owner.

questions.q: Explain [a concept from the JD] to a non-engineer.
questions.tip: Analogy first, then one level deeper.

questions.q: How do you review code? What do you look for?
questions.tip: Correctness, readability, tests, security, then style.

questions.q: Describe a time you improved performance or reliability.
questions.tip: Baseline number, what you changed, the new number.

questions.q: How do you write tests for code that's hard to test?
questions.tip: Seams, dependency injection, contract tests.

questions.q: Tell me about disagreeing with a technical decision.
questions.tip: Evidence, how you raised it, disagree-and-commit.

questions.q: Walk me through an analysis that changed a business decision.
questions.tip: Question, data, method, insight, decision, impact.

questions.q: How would you design an A/B test for [feature]?
questions.tip: Hypothesis, metric, sample size, duration, pitfalls (peeking, novelty).

questions.q: A metric moved unexpectedly. How do you find out why?
questions.tip: Data quality, seasonality, segments, recent launches.

questions.q: Write a SQL query to find the top 3 [items] per [group].
questions.tip: Window functions: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ...).

questions.q: How do you explain a model's results to non-technical stakeholders?
questions.tip: Business framing, one chart, confidence and limits.

questions.q: How do you handle missing or messy data?
questions.tip: Understand why it's missing, then impute, flag or drop with reason.

questions.q: Precision vs recall: which matters more for [use case]?
questions.tip: Tie to the cost of false positives vs false negatives.

questions.q: Tell me about a dashboard or metric you built that people actually used.
questions.tip: Who used it, for what decision, adoption.

questions.q: How would you detect fraud / churn / anomalies in [domain]?
questions.tip: Features, labels, baseline model, evaluation, monitoring.

questions.q: Walk me through a project in your portfolio.
questions.tip: Problem, research, options, decision, outcome; show your process.

questions.q: How do you handle feedback you disagree with?
questions.tip: Get to the underlying concern, test it, decide with evidence.

questions.q: Redesign [common app screen] for [user group].
questions.tip: Users, goals, constraints, sketches, how you'd validate.

questions.q: How do you measure whether a design is successful?
questions.tip: Task success, time on task, conversion, qualitative signals.

questions.q: Tell me about a time research changed your direction.
questions.tip: What you assumed, what you learned, what you changed.

questions.q: How do you work with engineers on edge cases and handoff?
questions.tip: Specs, states, design systems, early pairing.

questions.q: How do you balance user needs with business goals?
questions.tip: Show a concrete trade-off and how you resolved it.

questions.q: What does accessibility mean in your work?
questions.tip: Contrast, keyboard, screen readers, inclusive language.

questions.q: Walk me through a campaign you ran and its results.
questions.tip: Goal, audience, channel, creative, spend, result.

questions.q: How would you grow [our product] from 0 to 10,000 users?
questions.tip: ICP, channels to test, budget, metrics, iteration loop.

questions.q: Our CAC doubled. What do you look at?
questions.tip: Channel mix, conversion rates, competition, attribution changes.

questions.q: How do you decide which channels to invest in?
questions.tip: Test small, compare CAC/LTV and payback, scale winners.

questions.q: Tell me about an experiment that failed.
questions.tip: Hypothesis, result, what you learned, what you did next.

questions.q: How do you measure brand impact?
questions.tip: Branded search, share of voice, surveys, direct traffic.

questions.q: How do you work with product and sales teams?
questions.tip: Shared goals, regular feedback loops, a concrete example.

questions.q: Write a one-line positioning statement for our product.
questions.tip: For [user] who [need], [product] is [category] that [benefit].

questions.q: Sell me this pen / our product.
questions.tip: Ask questions first, find the need, then pitch to it.

questions.q: Walk me through your sales process.
questions.tip: Prospecting, discovery, demo, objections, close, handoff.

questions.q: Tell me about a deal you lost and why.
questions.tip: Honest reason, what you'd do differently.

questions.q: How do you handle the objection 'it's too expensive'?
questions.tip: Reframe on value and cost of inaction; never discount first.

questions.q: How did you perform against quota?
questions.tip: Numbers: attainment %, deal size, cycle length.

questions.q: A key customer is about to churn. What do you do?
questions.tip: Understand root cause, exec alignment, success plan.

questions.q: How do you prioritise your pipeline?
questions.tip: Qualification framework (e.g. MEDDIC/BANT) and deal stage.

questions.q: Tell me about building a relationship with a difficult client.
questions.tip: Listening, small wins, trust over time.

questions.q: Walk me through how you'd size a new market for us in 48 hours.
questions.tip: Structure first, quick data sources, sanity checks.

questions.q: Our CEO wants to cut costs 20% this quarter. How would you approach it?
questions.tip: Cost baseline, big buckets, quick wins vs structural moves.

questions.q: Tell me about a process you redesigned.
questions.tip: Before/after metrics, how you got buy-in.

questions.q: How do you run a project across several teams?
questions.tip: Clear owner, milestones, cadence, escalation path.

questions.q: Which of our metrics would you look at in your first week, and why?
questions.tip: Revenue drivers, unit economics, a leading indicator.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to influence senior leadership.
questions.tip: Data, framing for their goals, the decision made.

questions.q: How do you decide what NOT to do?
questions.tip: Strategy fit, opportunity cost, explicit trade-offs.

questions.q: Build a simple model: how many [units] do we need to break even?
questions.tip: Fixed costs / contribution margin; state assumptions.

questions.q: Walk me through the three financial statements and how they link.
questions.tip: Net income → cash flow → balance sheet.

questions.q: How would you build a forecast for a business with little history?
questions.tip: Drivers, comparable companies, scenarios.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you found an error in the numbers.
questions.tip: How you caught it, impact, the control you added.

questions.q: How do you value a company?
questions.tip: DCF, comparables, precedent transactions; when to use each.

questions.q: Explain a variance in the budget to a non-finance manager.
questions.tip: Plain language, drivers, what to do about it.

questions.q: What metrics would you track for a subscription business?
questions.tip: MRR, churn, CAC, LTV, payback, net revenue retention.

ask_them: What does success look like in the first 90 days?
Which metrics does this team own, and how are they trending?
What's the biggest challenge the last person in this role faced?
How are decisions made on this team?
What do you enjoy most about working here?
What are the next steps in the process?
